rubric.result: The objective promises four things and each one is in the diff. The closed vocabulary of a reading: `CoverageState` and the discriminated union `CoverageReading` in coverage-reading.ts (lines 50-55). Its line counter: `LineCount` in line-count.ts. Its error: `UnreadableArtifact` in unreadable-artifact.ts. Its port: `CoverageArtifacts` in coverage-artifacts.ts. The closing clause 'so nothing downstream has to represent an absent measure as an optional' holds: 'no-artifact' and 'unreadable-artifact' are members of the union, `lines`, `source` and `measuredAt` exist only inside the `measured` member, and no `?` or `| null` appears anywhere in the six files. The two behaviours the brief attaches to the objective are also production lines, not declarations: `percentage()` at line-count.ts:88 and the `total === 0` rule at coverage-reading.ts:59. Nothing the objective names is missing.

Compared name by name against the three Contract blocks and the three one-line declarations. line-count.ts: `static of(covered: number, total: number): LineCount`, `private constructor(readonly covered: number, readonly total: number)`, `percentage(): number` — same names, same order, same modifiers, same return types. coverage-reading.ts: `CoverageState` with the three members in the stated order; `CoverageReading` with the three variants and, inside `measured`, exactly `lines: LineCount`, `source: CoverageFormat`, `measuredAt: Date`; `CoverageReadings.of(lines, source, measuredAt): CoverageReading`, `noArtifact(): CoverageReading`, `unreadableArtifact(): CoverageReading` — all three static, all three answering the union type and not a narrowed member. coverage-artifacts.ts: `interface CoverageArtifacts { readingOf(repoPath: string): Promise<CoverageReading> }` — verbatim. coverage-format.ts declares the union with the three literal values `'istanbul' | 'lcov' | 'cobertura'`. repo-coverage.ts declares `interface RepoCoverage { id: string; reading: CoverageReading }`. unreadable-artifact.ts declares `class UnreadableArtifact extends Error {}`, exported, carrying no code, which is what 'named for what happens and carrying no code: one case, told apart by its class' asks for. The two prose sentences of the task that fix behaviour also hold: `percentage()` is `Math.round((this.covered / this.total) * 1000) / 10`, which is `covered / total` as a percentage rounded to one decimal, and `CoverageReadings.of` is the only place that decides `total === 0`, answering `CoverageReadings.noArtifact()` (line 59) so the three future format readers never repeat the rule.

Row by row. 'Formats: exactly three: istanbul, lcov, cobertura' — coverage-format.ts declares exactly those three literals and no fourth, and no JaCoCo member appears. 'Metric: lines only, covered / total, rounded to one decimal' — `LineCount` carries only line counters and `percentage()` rounds to one decimal. 'An artefact with no line counters does not count: the walk continues to the next candidate' — `CoverageReadings.of` answers `noArtifact()` on `total === 0` instead of a measured reading, which is the half of that row this task owns; the walk itself is Task 2. 'Artefact that is not its format: the reader raises UnreadableArtifact' — the class is declared for the reader to raise. 'New server code lives under server/src/coverage/, one concept per module' — all six paths are under that directory, one concept each. 'Spanish is only for UI copy; identifiers, comments, test names and diagnostics in English' — every identifier and every vocabulary member is English, and no diagnostic string exists in the diff. Rows with no subject here, and therefore no finding: Route, Candidate order, 'No candidate counts', Order of the ranking, Measure date, Cache key — all six are Task 2 and later. No row is implemented with a different value, and none is reopened.

ct's five documents, then this repo's yardstick. conventions/defects.md, its four rules answered one by one. (1) Closed vocabulary: conforms and is the point of the task. `CoverageFormat` and `CoverageState` are closed unions of string literals, not strings compared by hand; the absent state and the failure state are members of `CoverageReading` rather than optionals, which is exactly 'an absent state is a member of the vocabulary, not an optional'; the union is discriminated by `state`, so a downstream dispatch fails at the type checker if a member is added; no boolean stands in for the vocabulary and no catch-all branch exists in this diff, because there is no dispatch in it yet. (2) Raw map as the return value of logic: no subject. The three factories of `CoverageReadings` return values of the declared union type, and `RepoCoverage` is a declared interface, not a map read by key lookup; nothing in the diff hands a bare object across two of its own functions. (3) Two fields that have to agree: no subject. `state` is the single discriminant and the three measured fields live only inside the `measured` member, so an absent measure cannot carry a stale percentage or date. No sentinel: there is no 0 % for 'unmeasured', no empty string, no epoch date — this is the defect the desired end state names ('Neither is ever reported as 0 %') and the type shape forecloses it. `LineCount.covered` and `LineCount.total` are a counter pair, not two fields that have to agree. (4) Error named for what happens, not for where: conforms. `UnreadableArtifact` names the event, not the module that raises it, and carries no code. It extends `Error` rather than a fitter parent because the coverage domain has no error root yet and the only existing error type, `ApiError` in server/src/api/errors.ts, sits in the boundary layer that conventions/architecture.md forbids the domain to import; the brief closes this shape as well. conventions/style.md: all six modules are new, so they are born conforming and take no debt exemption — no comment and no docstring in any of the 51 added lines, every identifier in English, and every function hangs off a type (`LineCount.of`, `LineCount.percentage`, the three statics of `CoverageReadings`) with no function at module level. The hosts this repo already has, server/src/repos.ts and server/src/api/routes.ts, are full of docstrings and module-level functions; the new tree correctly does not copy that debt, and no new concept was placed inside an old file to inherit it. conventions/architecture.md: applies in full, all six are `(create)`. This is a domain layer and it knows nobody — the only imports in the diff are `./coverage-reading.js`, `./line-count.js` and `./coverage-format.js`, all siblings; there is no input/output, no serialization and no import of application or infrastructure. `CoverageArtifacts` is a port declared in the domain for infrastructure to implement, which is where architecture.md puts ports. 'One concept per module' holds: `CoverageState`, `CoverageReading` and `CoverageReadings` share coverage-reading.ts and pass that document's yardstick — delete `CoverageReading` and neither the state alias nor the factory is left with a meaning of its own. No use case, policy, adapter, boundary model or entrypoint exists in this diff, so those sections have no subject. conventions/decisions.md: the `total === 0` rule is written once, in `CoverageReadings.of`, which is what the brief demands so the three readers never repeat it. One wrinkle to declare rather than count: `CoverageState` restates the same three-member partition that the `state` discriminants of the `CoverageReading` union already declare, which decisions.md lists as an antipattern ('the same partition of a closed vocabulary declared in more than one place'). The brief's `Contract (server/src/coverage/coverage-reading.ts)` block declares both verbatim, so the diff could not drop it without failing item 3. Per the rubric's clash clause this is declared and not counted as a finding: the defect, if it is one, is in the plan, and the plan is not what is being judged. conventions/testing.md: no test in this commit, and that is the document's own rule, not an evasion — 'what is inside the domain is covered along that path, not with tests of its own', and its single exception, 'a value with validation of its own that cannot be reached any other way', does not fire here: `LineCount.of` validates nothing, and the one rule that does decide something, `total === 0`, sits in `CoverageReadings.of`, reachable from the application path of Task 2. This repo's yardstick, from AGENTS.md as §3 names it: relative imports in `server/` carry the `.js` suffix — all four import lines do ('./coverage-reading.js', './line-count.js', './coverage-format.js'); code always in English — yes; author names and emails never leave the server — no such field exists in the diff; `web/` never imports from `server/` — `web/` is untouched; the server never mutates a clone and never fetches — the diff performs no input/output at all. Exemplars: the roles do not line up file for file, because routes.ts, repos.ts and Heat.tsx are a route, a filesystem reader and a React block while these six are domain values; the idiom they do share, the `.js` suffix and English identifiers, the diff follows. No finding under this item.
